title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. C2-C8 are out of scope for this plan because they require 12 datasets and would take hours; the code is dataset-agnostic if extended.

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (reimplementation of arXiv:2510.13352, Sec. 4).

Pipeline (per feature j, per sample i):
  1. Bin center selection via equal-frequency binning on OBSERVED values only:
       c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)), k = 1..nbins   (Eq. 4)
     => centers are evenly-spaced percentiles from min (0th) to max (100th).
  2. Proximity assignment: each observed value is assigned to its NEAREST bin
     center (Voronoi cell): b_{i,j} = argmin_k |x_{i,j} - c_{j,k}|          (Eq. 5)
  3. One-hot encoding of observed features; concatenate over features       (Eqs. 6-7)
  4. Missing values: three-level cascading fallback with kernel mean embedding:
       Level 1 (intersection): mean one-hot over samples matching ALL observed
             features of i (restricted to matches with feature j observed)  (Eqs. 8-10)
       Level 2 (union): mean one-hot over samples matching ANY observed
             feature of i (restricted to matches with feature j observed)   (Eqs. 11-12)
       Level 3 (global prior): bin frequency distribution of feature j     (Eqs. 13-14)
  5. Proximity kernel: K(x_m, x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n                        (Eq. 15)
"""
import numpy as np


def fit_bins(X, nbins):
    """Equal-frequency bin centers per feature from observed values (Eq. 4).

    Returns:
      centers: list of length d; centers[j] is an array of nbins bin centers,
               or None if feature j has no observed values.
      priors:  (d, nbins) global prior bin frequencies p_{j,k} (Eq. 13);
               uniform 1/nbins for entirely-missing features.
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    # evenly-spaced percentiles from 0 to 100 (paper Eq. 4: (k-1)*100/(nbins-1))
    qs = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins)
    centers, priors = [], np.zeros((d, nbins))
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            priors[j] = 1.0 / nbins  # uniform prior fallback
        else:
            centers.append(np.percentile(obs, qs))
            # global prior p_{j,k} = (# samples in bin k) / (# observed) (Eq. 13)
            b = _assign_to_centers(obs, centers[j])
            priors[j] = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins) / obs.size
    return centers, priors


def _assign_to_centers(values, centers):
    """Assign values to nearest center; ties break to the lowest bin index."""
    dist = np.abs(values[:, None] - centers[None, :])
    return np.argmin(dist, axis=1)


def assign_bins(X, centers, nbins):
    """Proximity assignment (Eq. 5). Returns B (n, d) int; -1 where missing."""
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        obs_mask = ~np.isnan(X[:, j])
        if centers[j] is None:
            continue
        B[obs_mask, j] = _assign_to_centers(X[obs_mask, j], centers[j])
    return B


def compute_fallback_encodings(B, priors, nbins):
    """Fill encodings for missing entries via the 3-level cascading fallback.

    Args:
      B: (n, d) bin assignments, -1 for missing.
      priors: (d, nbins) global prior distributions (Eq. 13).
    Returns:
      H: (n, d, nbins) encoding; one-hot for observed entries, probability
         vectors (summing to 1) for missing entries.
      level_counts: dict with counts of missing entries resolved at each level.
    """
    n, d = B.shape
    obs = B >= 0
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins))
    # one-hot encodings for observed entries (Eq. 6)
    ii, jj = np.nonzero(obs)
    H[ii, jj, B[ii, jj]] = 1.0

    # match[i, m, l] = True iff feature l is observed for sample i and sample m
    # falls in the same bin as sample i (b_{m,l} = b_{i,l}, Eq. 8; implies m
    # observed for l since bins are >= 0).
    eq = B[:, None, :] == B[None, :, :]          # (n, n, d)
    match = eq & obs[:, None, :]                 # i observed at l and equal bins

    not_i = ~np.eye(n, dtype=bool)
    # S1(i): match on ALL observed features of i (Eq. 9)
    all_match = (match | ~obs[:, None, :]).all(axis=2) & not_i   # (n, n)
    # S2(i): match on ANY observed feature of i (Eq. 11)
    any_match = match.any(axis=2) & not_i                        # (n, n)

    level_counts = {"level1": 0, "level2": 0, "level3": 0}
    miss_idx = np.argwhere(~obs)
    for i, j in miss_idx:
        obs_j = obs[:, j]
        # Level 1: intersection matches that have feature j observed (Eq. 10)
        s1 = all_match[i] & obs_j
        if s1.any():
            H[i, j] = H[s1, j].mean(axis=0)
            level_counts["level1"] += 1
            continue
        # Level 2: union matches that have feature j observed (Eq. 12)
        s2 = any_match[i] & obs_j
        if s2.any():
            H[i, j] = H[s2, j].mean(axis=0)
            level_counts["level2"] += 1
            continue
        # Level 3: global prior (Eq. 14)
        H[i, j] = priors[j]
        level_counts["level3"] += 1
    return H, level_counts


def build_representation(X, nbins):
    """Full pipeline: returns Z (n, d*nbins) and diagnostics dict."""
    n, d = X.shape
    centers, priors = fit_bins(X, nbins)
    B = assign_bins(X, centers, nbins)
    H, level_counts = compute_fallback_encodings(B, priors, nbins)
    Z = H.reshape(n, d * nbins)
    diag = {
        "nbins": nbins,
        "n_missing_entries": int((~np.isnan(X)).sum().__rsub__(X.size)),
        "fallback_level_counts": level_counts,
        "bin_centers_per_feature": {
            int(j): (None if centers[j] is None
                     else [round(float(c), 6) for c in centers[j]])
            for j in range(d)
        },
    }
    return Z, diag


def proximity_kernel(Z, d):
    """K = (1/d) Z Z^T (Eq. 15)."""
    return (Z @ Z.T) / d

"""K-means clustering evaluation with NMI (paper Sec. 5.1 evaluation protocol).

K-means is applied to the kernel representation Z with the number of clusters
set to the ground-truth number of classes; NMI is averaged over 10 runs.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score


def evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds, n_init=10):
    """Run KMeans once per seed; return per-seed NMI, mean and std."""
    nmis = []
    for s in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init,
                    random_state=s)
        labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
        nmis.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)))
    return {
        "per_seed_nmi": nmis,
        "mean_nmi": float(np.mean(nmis)),
        "std_nmi": float(np.std(nmis)),
    }


def search_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, nbins_grid, seeds, n_init=10):
    """Evaluate every nbins in the grid; select the best by mean NMI."""
    from src.proximity_kernel import build_representation

    results = {}
    diagnostics = {}
    for nb in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, nb)
        res = evaluate_representation(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds, n_init=n_init)
        results[nb] = res
        diagnostics[nb] = diag
        print(f"nbins={nb}: mean NMI={res['mean_nmi']:.4f} "
              f"(std={res['std_nmi']:.4f}) fallback={diag['fallback_level_counts']}")
    best_nbins = max(results, key=lambda nb: results[nb]["mean_nmi"])
    return best_nbins, results[best_nbins], results, diagnostics

audit_summary: The target claim C1 is reproduced with the proposed proximity kernel, not a baseline: equal-frequency/percentile bin centers from observed values only, Voronoi nearest-center assignment, one-hot encoding, the three-level intersection/union/prior fallback via kernel mean embedding, and K-means with the ground-truth K=2 evaluated by sklearn NMI, averaged over 10 seeds with the nbins grid {2,3,4,6,8} — the full protocol for this dataset, on the correct UCI Hepatitis (155x19, 2 classes, 167 missing = 5.67%, matching Table 2). A clean re-run from scratch exits 0 in ~6 s and reproduces NMI = 0.22891 (nbins=2, std=0), i.e. the paper's 0.2289 to four decimals; no paper number appears in any source file and the value is computed from data, so there is no hardcoding or echoed constant. Two caveats for a researcher: (1) the decisive design choice is the percentile grid (A13), which for nbins=2 degenerates to centers at min/max and a midrange split rather than a true equal-frequency split — the alternative convention would give a different number, so the exact four-decimal agreement is either strong evidence the authors used the same Eq. (4) convention or a lucky coincidence, and an independent check with the alternative convention would settle it; (2) the second decisive choice is A8 (KME sums restricted to matches with the target feature observed), which is undisclosed in the paper, and level 3 of the cascade is never exercised on Hepatitis (0/167), so that branch is unvalidated. Clustering is performed on Z with Euclidean KMeans rather than on the Eq. (15) kernel matrix (A14), which is equivalent up to per-row norm scaling and does not change the method. Only C1 was attempted; claims C2-C8 (12-dataset average, best/second-best counts, baselines, the O(nd + d n log n) complexity claim) were not evaluated, so the paper's headline average NMI 0.4245 and 10/12 count remain unverified.

requirement_check.evidence: fit_bins() computes centers per feature from obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:,j]), j] only; missing entries never influence centers. (Caveat: with the chosen grid, nbins=2 yields the min/max pair, so the split is at midrange, not median — the 'equal-frequency' reading holds only approximately for nbins>=3.)

qs = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins) with np.percentile(..., qs) (linear interpolation, A2); i.e. percentiles at (k-1)*100/(nbins-1) per implementer assumption A13, stated to match paper Eq. (4) and the 'cj,1/cj,nbins are min/max' sentence.
_assign_to_centers uses np.argmin(|x - c|) over centers, deterministic tie-break to lowest index (A3); produces B in {0..nbins-1} for observed, -1 for missing.
H[ii,jj,B[ii,jj]] = 1.0 for observed entries and Z = H.reshape(n, d*nbins); verified structurally in smoke() (per-feature encodings sum to 1).
compute_fallback_encodings implements an explicit 3-level cascade (level1 intersection -> level2 union -> level3 global prior) with per-level counters reported per nbins in metrics.json.

all_match(S1) requires bin agreement on every feature observed in i, excluding self; H[i,j] = mean of one-hot rows of matching samples restricted to those with feature j observed (A8, disclosed in ledger and metrics notes). 61/167 missing entries resolved at level 1 for nbins=2.
any_match(S2) = records matching i on at least one observed feature, again restricted to j-observed matches; 106/167 entries resolved at level 2 for nbins=2, so the branch is exercised and dominant.

Code path H[i,j] = priors[j] (bin-frequency global prior, uniform for all-missing features) exists, but level3 count is 0 for every nbins on Hepatitis, so this branch was never executed or validated by the run.

proximity_kernel(Z,d) returns (Z @ Z.T)/d exactly as Eq. (15); however it is only used in the smoke test — clustering runs Euclidean KMeans on Z (A14), which equals kernel k-means for the linear kernel Z Z^T up to per-row norm variation, so this is a minor, disclosed deviation rather than a substitution.

src/cluster.py uses sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=K=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10) and sklearn normalized_mutual_info_score (arithmetic-mean variant, A5) on the full 155-sample Hepatitis set (transductive, A10).
SEEDS = list(range(10)); per_nbins_per_seed_nmi has 10 values per nbins and mean/std are averaged over them (std=0 for the selected nbins=2 because all 10 seeds yield the identical partition).
NBINS_GRID = [2,3,4,6,8]; search_nbins evaluates every value and selects the max mean NMI (A9); all five per-nbins means are logged (0.2289, 0.1718, 0.2097, 0.2104, 0.1967).

No timing/scaling experiment was run for the complexity claim, and the fallback builds an (n, n, d) boolean tensor (eq, match), i.e. O(n^2 d) memory/time — quadratic, not linear, in n; this implementation would not scale to the Adult-size dataset cited in the paper.
Observed entries are strict one-hot, so a complete sample has exactly d nonzeros out of d*nbins; smoke() asserts H.sum(axis=2)==1 for all rows and Z has no NaN/inf.
